LanguageData.CC_Settings_InspectPortrait: A large portrait at the inspect pane
LanguageData.CC_Settings_InspectPortrait_Tip: With one person selected on the map (a colonist, a slave, a prisoner, a visitor, a raider), a large portrait of them stands above the inspect pane at the bottom left, facing the front, with their name and the name the colony knows them by. While a tab is open (Bio, Gear, Health, Log) it is hidden and the tab has the room. Drag its top right corner to make it larger or smaller; click it for their card. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_InspectPortrait: The selected person's face, large, above the inspect pane.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_InspectPortraitSize_Tip: How wide and tall the portrait at the inspect pane is, from 96 to 360. Dragging its top right corner sets this too. Where the screen has less room, it is drawn smaller.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_InspectPortraitSize: Its width and height on the screen; dragging its corner sets it too.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitHeadgear_Tip: On, every portrait Rimfolk draws (letters, event cards, the colonist card, the lists and the large portrait) shows the helmet or hat a person wears, as the game draws them. Off, the face and hair without it, so a person looks the same whatever they wear on their head.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitHeadgear: Portraits show helmets and hats as worn; off, a face stays the same whatever they wear.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitClothes_Tip: On, portraits show the clothes and armour on the body as worn. Off, the body without them, so new armour changes nothing in the picture.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitClothes: Portraits show the clothes and armour they wear.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitPoses_Tip: A person's portrait shows how they hold themselves: the chin up for the proud (a proud trait, a council seat, the head of a people, a title), the head a little down for the sad or grieving, a lean for the angry (a break, a fresh quarrel), turned half away for the shy in letters and cards, a slight stoop for the old, the head low for a prisoner, and the dead drawn grey. A pose stays for at least an hour of the game unless a break, death or captivity changes it. The large portraits and those in letters and cards take a pose; the large portraits always face the front, and the small ones in lists face the front too. Two people side by side in a letter or a tie face each other either way.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitPoses: Portraits show the proud, the sad, the angry, the shy, the old, prisoners and the dead each their own way.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitsMove_Tip: The large portrait at the inspect pane and the one on the colonist card breathe and sway a little, always facing the front. They hold still while the game is paused. The small portraits in lists never move.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitsMove: The large portraits breathe and sway a little; still while paused.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitLibrary_Tip: Portraits show a painted picture from the library where one may stand for the person: a picture made for that colonist (pinned to them by name), else the one closest to how they look (skin, hair colour and length, beard, build and the age of their clothes). A picture is always of their own kind, sex and age band, with a skin of the same or the next tone (an unusual skin, such as green or blue, only one of a near colour); where the library has none, they keep the game's own face. The picture is chosen the first time it is needed and kept for good: injuries, a new haircut or new clothes don't change it. A child gets a new one when they grow into the next stage (a baby, a toddler, a child, a grown-up). Right-click the large portrait to choose another picture. A race or xenotype with no pictures of its own keeps the game's own face, never another kind's picture, so you can see which kinds still need pictures (they are listed in missing.csv in your library folder). A colonist's picture is never given to anyone else. The pictures come from the player's own pack of painted portraits; the library is empty until it is added. Off, every portrait is the game's own face.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitLibrary: Portraits show a painted picture for each person, chosen once and kept.
LanguageData.CC_SetTip_PortraitPick: Which people get a painted picture. "The closest": everyone the library has a picture for that may stand for them (their own kind, sex, age band and skin tone), even if it doesn't look much like them. "Only close ones": only where a picture looks close to them; the rest keep the game's own face. Pictures pinned to a colonist and pictures chosen by hand show either way.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitPick_Closest: Everyone gets the picture closest to their looks, of their own kind, sex, age band and skin tone.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitPick_OnlyClose: Only pictures that look close to the person are shown; the others keep the game's own face.
LanguageData.CC_SetTip_PortraitShare: A painted picture of one of your people (colonists, slaves, prisoners) is theirs alone, and a faction leader's, a titled noble's or one of the colony's named contacts' is theirs alone while they live. Everyone else (raiders, traders, visitors, guests) gets a picture nobody holds where there is one. This says whether they may get one another stranger already holds when none is free. "Never": no, they keep the game's own drawing. "When not seen together": only while the stranger holding it is on no map, and if two with the same picture meet on the maps, the one who got it later gets another or the game's drawing. "Always": yes, for a small library. Pictures of a special look (conjoined twins, wings) may always be shared among strangers.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitShare_Never: A stranger only gets a picture nobody else holds; otherwise the game's own drawing.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitShare_NotTogether: Strangers may share a picture while they are never on the maps at the same time.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitShare_Always: Strangers may share pictures freely, for a small library.
LanguageData.CC_SetTip_PortraitBackdrop: Behind the person in the large portrait (a painted picture, and the game's own drawing where "Backdrop behind the game's own drawing too" is on), a painted backdrop of where the person is: indoors the kind of room, the colony's age and what is in the room; outdoors the kind of land; darker and cooler at night. "As painted" shows it as it was painted. "Lightly softened" blurs it a little and makes it slightly darker and less colourful. "Softened" blurs it more and makes it darker, so the person stands out more. "Plain" shows no backdrop, only the portrait's own colour.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitBackdrop_AsPainted: The backdrop of where they are, as it was painted.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitBackdrop_LightlySofte: The backdrop a little blurred, darker and less colourful.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitBackdrop_Softened: The backdrop clearly blurred and darker, so the person stands out.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitBackdrop_Plain: No backdrop: the portrait's own colour behind the person.
LanguageData.CC_SetTip_PortraitOutline: A line round the person in the large portrait's painted picture, so they stand apart from the backdrop: a soft dark shadow just round them, a faint pale edge and a thin dark line, following their shape. "Subtle" is light, "Stronger" firmer.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitOutline_Subtle: A light shadow and thin line round the person.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitOutline_Stronger: A firmer shadow and line round the person.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitFolder_Tip: The folder that holds your painted portraits: its records.xml, which describes every picture, and the pictures in its subfolders. It can be a folder you keep in step between computers (a cloud drive). Paste its full path, for example C:\Users\you\Google Drive\Rimfolk Portraits, then press "Reload the library". Rimfolk reads it when the game starts, and writes missing.csv into it: the people, rooms and land it needed a picture for and found none, for the next batches. Empty: no folder (pictures from mods are still used).
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitFolder: Where your painted portraits are kept; Rimfolk also writes there what it found missing.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitFolder_ReloadTip: Read the folder's records.xml and its pictures' names again, after adding a batch. Pictures already kept by your people stay theirs.
LanguageData.CC_SetTip_PortraitDelete: What happens to the files when you delete a painted picture or a backdrop for good (right-click the large portrait, "Delete this picture for good..."). "Move it to the bin": the picture and its expressions, or the backdrop and its depth map, are moved into the folder "deleted pictures" beside the library folder, in a folder of their batch, so you can look at them once more before you empty it. "Delete the files": they are deleted at once. Either way the picture's record is taken out of records.xml and its name is written into deleted.csv in the library folder, so the portrait scripts never copy, record or check it again, and whoever held it gets another picture.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitDelete_Bin: A picture deleted for good is moved into the folder "deleted pictures" beside the library folder.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitDelete_Delete: A picture deleted for good has its files deleted at once.
LanguageData.CC_PortraitFolder_None: No portrait library folder is set.
LanguageData.CC_PortraitFolder_Failed: Portraits: the library folder {FOLDER} could not be read ({WHY}), so its pictures are not used for now. Rimfolk tries again in a minute.
LanguageData.CC_PortraitFolder_Missing: {COUNT} pictures named in records.xml are not in the folder and are left out.
LanguageData.CC_PortraitFolder_Alive: Also {FACES} expressions of those portraits (eyes closed, a smile, a frown, pain) and {DEPTHS} depth maps of the backdrops, for the large portrait.
LanguageData.CC_PortraitNeed_NoStage: none of their sex, age and skin tone
LanguageData.CC_PortraitNeed_NoRoom: no backdrop of this kind of room
LanguageData.CC_PortraitNeed_NoFree: no free picture: those that fit are other people's
LanguageData.CC_PortraitNeed_NoLook: no picture of their kind shows this look
LanguageData.CC_PortraitNeed_NoSpecialLook: a special look no picture of their kind shows, so the game's own drawing
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitBackdropGame: Backdrop behind the game's own drawing too
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitBackdropGame_Tip: When the library has no painted picture for someone and the large portrait shows the game's own drawing of them, the backdrop of where they are stands behind it too, softened and darkened at night as the setting "Backdrop" says, with a soft shadow behind them. Off: the game's drawing stays on the portrait's own colour, and painted pictures keep their backdrop.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitBackdropGame: The backdrop stands behind the game's own drawing as well as behind painted pictures.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitLightTint: Tint the person to the room's light
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitLightTint_Tip: The person in the large portrait's painted picture takes on a little of the backdrop's colour (about a fifth), so a warm firelit room makes them warmer and a cold night cooler.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitLightTint: The person takes on a little of the backdrop's light.
LanguageData.CC_SetTip_PortraitDepth: While the mouse is over the large portrait, the backdrop moves a few pixels away from it and the person a little toward it, with their shadow on the wall in between, so the picture seems to have depth. When the mouse leaves, it eases back to the middle. Where a backdrop has a depth map, the near things in it move apart from the far wall too. The picture is drawn a little larger than the frame so its edge never shows, and the person stays on the bottom edge. "Subtle" moves it a little, "Stronger" more. Off: the large portrait stays still under the mouse.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitDepth_Off: The large portrait stays still under the mouse.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitDepth_Subtle: The backdrop and the person shift a little apart as the mouse moves over the large portrait.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitDepth_Stronger: The backdrop and the person shift clearly apart as the mouse moves over the large portrait.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitFaces_Tip: Where a painted picture has its expressions painted too (eyes closed, a smile, a frown, pain), the large portrait uses them: the person blinks every few seconds, keeps their eyes closed while asleep or unconscious, smiles while their mood is high and frowns while it is well under their minor break line, and for a while shows pain after being hurt or while in pain, a frown after the death of someone close, and a smile after good news. A change of mood holds for at least a minute, and one face fades into the next. A picture without these expressions stays as it is. Still while the game is paused.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitFaces: The large portrait blinks and shows mood, pain and news where those expressions are painted.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PortraitBackdropAlive_Tip: Behind the person in the large portrait, outdoors under the open sky, the map's weather falls lightly over the backdrop: rain, snow, fog or dust, as the weather is. Indoors, where the backdrop shows a hearth or a fire, or a fire is lit in the room, a soft warm light flickers over the lower part of the backdrop. Only the large portrait shows it, and it holds still while the game is paused.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_PortraitBackdropAlive: The weather outdoors and a fire's flicker indoors show on the large portrait's backdrop.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_TipLibrary: {PAWN_nameDef}: click for their card, right-click to choose another painted picture, keep one for training or delete one for good.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_GripTip: Drag to make the portrait larger or smaller.

LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteBusy: the last one is still being deleted
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteReading: the library folder is being read
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteNoBin: the library folder has no folder above it for the bin; choose "Delete the files" in the settings
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteWhat: The painted picture {FILE} in the library folder will be deleted for good.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteBackdropWhat: The backdrop {FILE} in the library folder will be deleted for good.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteWhatDepth: Its depth map goes with it.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteHeld: It is held now by {NAMES}. Whoever holds it gets another picture by the usual rules: a picture made for them first, then the closest one nobody holds, else the game's own drawing.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteBackdropShown: It is shown now behind {PAWN_nameDef}. The large portrait then chooses another backdrop for where they are, else a plain one.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteToBin: Its files are moved into the bin, the folder {BIN} beside the library folder, which you empty yourself.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteRecord: Its record is taken out of records.xml and its name is written into deleted.csv, so the portrait scripts never copy, record or check it again.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteNoUndo: This can't be undone in the game.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteGone: {NAME} is no longer in the library, so nothing was deleted.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteNoLonger: {COUNT} more no longer in the world
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteFailed: Could not delete {FILE}: {WHY}. Nothing was changed. A cloud drive may be holding the file for a moment; try again shortly.
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeleteWhyNoRecords: the library folder has no records.xml
LanguageData.CC_Portrait_DeletedDepth: Its depth map went with it.
